anomalies.observed: On the root sheet, the TACH node (the bottom terminal of the 10 kΩ pull-up R6, which also carries the TACH global label going to U2.2/U3.2 and, through R4/D1, to the fan J2.3) is joined by a long diagonal wire to the +5V rail at the LM1117 output (U1.3 / C2 top). The signal net TACH is therefore tied directly to the +5V supply.
anomalies.expected: TACH is an open-collector tachometer input that should be pulled up to a single rail through R6 only; it must not be hard-connected to the +5V supply rail. A data/sense net should never be merged with a power net.

evidence.quote: R6 10K, top terminal 'VCC', bottom terminal 'TACH'; a diagonal wire leaves the TACH node and runs to the '+5V' arrow at the LM1117-5.0 output (U1.3) on the column-5/6 tile (root sheet)
J2 FAN pin 3 'TACH_IN' -> R4 1K -> D1 5V1 -> 'TACH' global label; U2/U3 pin 2 'TACH'

anomalies.impact: The tachometer line is pinned at +5V, so the MCU can never see the fan's open-collector pulses and RPM feedback is lost; the fan's tach output also fights the rail through R4, and if VCC (the raw rail feeding R6) exceeds 5 V, current flows through R6 into the +5V net.

parsed.summary: The drawing shows the TACH signal net bridged directly to the +5V supply rail via a diagonal wire at the LM1117 output, which is a signal-to-power merge that would disable fan tachometer feedback; the rest of the fan drive (PMOS high-side switch, NPN level shifter, PWM/TACH series resistors and 5.1 V clamp) is consistent with an ATtiny-driven fan controller.
